summary.text: Andy Bowline is the Democratic candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 31 in the November 3, 2026 general election, running against incumbent Dana Caudill Jones (R).
A Winston-Salem stay-at-home father and former health tech company co-founder, he says he is running to give voters a choice in a heavily Republican district.

paragraphs.text: Andy Bowline earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Texas at Austin and a graduate degree from Wake Forest University.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he described himself as a stay-at-home dad and former health tech CEO who co-founded a health tech company, worked as a software developer and nonprofit consultant, and earned an MBA at Wake Forest.
He said he lives in Winston-Salem with his family and has two children in North Carolina public schools.
Bowline advanced to the general election after the Democratic primary was canceled.
In the survey, he named public schools, health care access, corporate accountability and fair maps as the issues he cares about.
He said he would seek accountability and audits for corporate tax breaks, oppose voucher funding he said mostly goes to families already in private school, and protect Medicaid expansion.
